tasks.title: Biodiversity corridor priorities
tasks.instruction: You must answer this question. Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: Your class has listened to a radio discussion about a biodiversity corridor project being planned in your region. The project aims to connect green spaces so that urban wildlife can move safely between them. You have made the notes below.

promptBlocks.heading: Priorities for the biodiversity corridor
listItems: creating safe crossing points across busy roads
planting native vegetation along the corridor
involving local residents in monitoring wildlife

promptBlocks.heading: Some opinions expressed in the discussion:
paragraphs: If animals can't cross roads safely, the corridor is useless. Safe crossings are the most urgent priority.
Native plants provide food and shelter for wildlife. Without them, the corridor won't attract the species it's meant to protect.
If residents help monitor, they'll feel ownership and the corridor will be better looked after in the long term.

promptBlocks.text: Write an essay for your tutor discussing two of the priorities in your notes. You should explain which priority you think is more important for the success of the biodiversity corridor, giving reasons in support of your answer. You may, if you wish, make use of the opinions expressed in the discussion, but you should use your own words as far as possible.

tasks.title: Proposal for community engagement
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: The regional wildlife trust is planning a biodiversity corridor and wants to ensure that local residents are actively involved in its creation and maintenance. The trust has invited proposals from community groups for how this engagement should be organised.

Write a proposal for the wildlife trust. In your proposal, you should:

• recommend two specific ways to involve residents in the corridor project
• explain how these activities would benefit both the wildlife and the local community
• suggest how the trust could measure the success of community engagement

tasks.title: Email to programme coordinator
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.subject: Biodiversity corridor – concerns about access
paragraphs: I am writing on behalf of the GreenLink Residents' Association to express some concerns about the proposed biodiversity corridor. While we fully support the aim of protecting urban wildlife, we are worried that the planned route may restrict access to a popular walking path that many residents use daily.

I would appreciate your analysis of this potential implication. Could you also suggest what action the project organisers could take to address our concerns while still achieving the corridor's goals?
I look forward to your response.

promptBlocks.text:
Write an email to Maya Johansson. In your email, you should:

• acknowledge the concern and explain the reasoning behind the planned route
• analyse one potential implication for residents if the route is changed
• propose an action the project could take to address the concern while maintaining the corridor's effectiveness

tasks.title: Review of a wildlife corridor
tasks.instruction: Answer one of the following questions (2–4). Write 220–260 words in an appropriate style.

promptBlocks.text: You see this announcement on an English-language nature website.

promptBlocks.heading: Reviews wanted: Urban wildlife corridors
paragraphs: Have you visited an urban wildlife corridor – a green route designed to help animals move safely through a city? We want to hear about your experience.

Write a review for our website. Describe the corridor and what wildlife you observed. Evaluate how well it balanced the needs of wildlife with the convenience of people using the area. Would you recommend this corridor as a model for other cities? Why or why not?
The best reviews will be published on our website.
